etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English caboche, cabage (“cabbage”; “a certain fish”), a borrowing from Anglo-Norman caboche (“head”), a northern variant of caboce, of uncertain origin. Some authorities derive it from Latin caput (“head”), others from ca- (said to be an expressive prefix) + boce (“hump; bump”) (whence English boss).

definitions.definition: (by extension) Any of various cultivars of the species Brassica oleracea.
An edible plant (Brassica oleracea var. capitata) having a head of green leaves.
(uncountable, vegetable) The leaves of this plant eaten as a vegetable.
(countable, offensive) A person with severely reduced mental capacities due to brain damage.
Used as a term of endearment.

quote.citation: 2009, Tom Stoppard, Helen Rappaport, The Cherry Orchard, translation of Вишнëвый сад ("Vishniovy sad") by Anton Chekhov, published 1904, page 31:
quote.text: If you deceive me, Yasha, I don't know if my nerves could stand it. YASHA (kissing her) My little cabbage! Of course, a girl must know her place.

definitions.definition: (uncountable, slang) Marijuana leaf, the part that is not smoked but from which cannabutter can be extracted.
A terminal bud of certain palm trees, used for food.
A cabbage palmetto (Sabal palmetto), a palm of the southeastern US coasts and nearby islands.
(intransitive) To form a head like that of the cabbage.
(intransitive, slang) To do nothing; to idle; veg out.

quote.citation: 2006, Steve Mckevitt, Why the World Is Full of Useless Things, page 38:
quote.text: How effective the project was is a moot point, because there were never any studies carried out to see whether children benefited from cabbaging in front of the TV rather than interacting with a teacher.

definitions.definition: (slang, African-American Vernacular) To be killed or murdered, such as by being shot in the head.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: Unclear. Perhaps from Dutch *kabbassen, from Old French cabasser (“put into a basket”), from cabas. Alternatively, perhaps from an earlier word *carbage (“shred”), a potential variant of *garbage (“wheat straw”).

definitions.definition: (slang) Scraps of cloth which are left after a garment has been cut out, which tailors traditionally kept.
(transitive) To embezzle or purloin; to pilfer, to steal.

quote.citation: 1733, Humphry Polesworth [pseudonym; John Arbuthnot], Alexander Pope, compiler, “Law is a Bottomless Pit. Or, The History of John Bull. […]. [The First Part.] Chapter X. Of John Bull’s Second Wife, and the Good Advice that She Gave Him.”, in Miscellanies, 2nd edition, volume II, London:  […]  Benjamin Motte, […], →OCLC, page 30:
quote.text: [Y]our Butler purloins your Liquor, and your Brevver ſells your Hogvvaſh;  […]  your Taylor, inſtead of Shreds, cabages vvhole Yards of Cloth;  […]

quote.citation: 1913, Joseph C[rosby] Lincoln, chapter VIII, in Mr. Pratt’s Patients, New York, N.Y., London: D[aniel] Appleton and Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: We toted in the wood and got the fire going nice and comfortable. Lord James still set in one of the chairs and Applegate had cabbaged the other and was hugging the stove.
